thread.title: Micron earnings show more big profit and sales gains, but stock dips slightly - MarketWatch

author: Jeremy C. Owens
title: Micron earnings show more big profit and sales gains, but stock dips slightly - MarketWatch
text:
Micron Technology Inc. continued to post huge gains in profit and revenue amid high memory-chip prices in a Wednesday earnings report, but it seemed those gains were already priced into the stock as shares dipped in late trading.
Micron MU, -0.51% profit more than doubled from the year before, while sales grew by 40%. Micron reported third-quarter net income of $3.82 billion, or $3.10 a share, on sales of $7.8 billion, up from $5.57 billion in the year-ago quarter. After adjustments for stock-based compensation and other effects, the company claimed earnings of $3.15 a share, up from $1.62 a share a year ago.
Analysts on average expected adjusted earnings of $3.13 cents a share on sales of $7.76 billion, according to FactSet, after Micron divulged updated expectations for the quarter late last month in a meeting with analysts. The company had increased its forecast to $3.12 to $3.16 a share on revenue of $7.7 billion to $7.8 billion, up from $2.76 to $2.90 a share on revenue of $7.2 billion to $7.6 billion.
Shares fell about 1% in late trading after numbers were released. Micron stock has been on a tear as memory prices have increased over the past couple of years, rising 91.4% in the past year as the S&P 500 index SPX, +0.17% has gained 13.4%.
Micron’s stock has been juiced by higher prices for its core product, computer memory, which Micron has attributed to demand from cloud-data centers, especially in China. However, the price of memory has attracted the attention of Chinese regulators , and analysts and companies — including tech titan Apple Inc. AAPL, +0.44% — have said of late that they expect the increase in prices to calm soon, potentially in the second half of the year .
Micron Chief Executive Sanjay Mehrotra — who has repeatedly said that the increased prices are part of a new demand environment that is not as transitory as previous memory cycles — did not sound concerned about that possibility in Wednesday’s announcement.
“We see ongoing momentum and healthy industry fundamentals in the fourth quarter to close out an exceptionally strong fiscal 2018,” Mehrotra said.
